title: When the Ember Falls
premise: When the old gods of Thornfell wake and begin answering prayers with fire, the kingdom's borders dissolve into warring shrine-states, and Mara Joubert — a runaway apprentice who knows every smuggler's path through the mountains — becomes the only guide anyone trusts. Hunted by the Ember Court, a new priesthood that burns heretics to feed the waking gods, Mara agrees to lead a disgraced inquisitor and a god-touched child to the Door at Thornfell's heart: the last passage out of a country that officially no longer exists. Along the way he must choose between saving himself and breaking the cycle that keeps the gods hungry. In the end, Mara seals the Door from the inside, trading his escape for the country's chance to be reborn — and walks out the other side as something no longer quite mortal.
about_author: O. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, belief, and the people who slip between both.

chapters.title: Salt on the Mountain Road
chapters.summary: Mara Joubert, POV. Fleeing his hedge-witch mistress after stealing her grimoire, Mara guides a salt caravan over the Thornfell pass using smuggler roads only he knows. The beat is wary competence — a man who survives by never being needed by anyone.

chapters.title: The First Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. At a roadside shrine, Mara witnesses a dying shepherd pray aloud — and the mountain answers with a pillar of green flame. The caravan scatters; Mara alone sees the god's face in the fire. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Reaching the lowlands, Mara finds the border garrison burned out and royal writs replaced by shrine-law. A herald declares Thornfell dissolved into the Ember Court's dominion. Beat: displacement — home erased while he was on the road.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Rope
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sera Vane, POV. Vane, stripped of office for doubting the Court's miracles, captures Mara as a suspected god-speaker but realizes he is her only map. She offers a bargain: guide me to the Door, and live. Beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual leverage.

chapters.title: What the Grimoire Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Studying his stolen grimoire by night, Mara discovers his mistress was once an Ember priestess who helped seal the gods away generations ago. Beat: betrayal reframed — his whole apprenticeship was preparation he never consented to.

chapters.title: The Child Who Hums to Stones
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. In a refugee column they find Pell, a mute child whose humming makes standing stones glow. The Court wants the child; so does something older. Vane, against instinct, refuses to hand Pell over. Beat: hardened justice bending toward mercy.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Justice
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. A smuggler captain who owes Mara a debt offers safe passage — then sells their route to the Court for amnesty. Mara executes him on the pass, outside any law. Beat: the price of survival paid in blood, and Mara's first taste of power's rot.

chapters.title: Ash Choir
chapters.summary: Pell, POV (rendered impressionistically). Taken briefly by the Court, Pell experiences the gods' hunger directly — prayers arriving like hands reaching down a well. Rescued mid-ritual, Pell speaks a first word: 'Door.' Beat: terror made intimate.

chapters.title: The High Shrine of Vess
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. Sheltering with mountain clans who still keep the old rites, Vane learns the Court doesn't worship the gods — it farms them, feeding them heretics to harvest power. Beat: her faith inverted; the law she served was the corruption all along.

chapters.title: Frostbound
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. A blizzard traps the trio in a cave where the grimoire's sealed pages finally open, revealing the Door's location — and its price: it opens only for one who gives up what they most want to keep. Beat: quiet intimacy and mounting dread around a dying fire.

chapters.title: The Court's Offer
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. The Ember Hierophant corners them with an offer: guide us to the Door and receive wealth, pardon, a name. Mara nearly accepts. Beat: temptation rendered honestly — survival has always been his religion.

chapters.title: Crossing the Burnt Vale
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. The party crosses a valley the gods consumed overnight, walking between still-warm corpses of pilgrims who prayed too loudly. Beat: horror as consequence — every answered prayer is a debt collected elsewhere.

chapters.title: Old Debts, Old Names
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. They reach his former mistress's hidden hut and find her waiting, unaged, sustained by the gods' return. She reveals Mara was chosen as a child to be the Door's key. Beat: rage and grief — his life was never his own.

chapters.title: The Turning of Sera Vane
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. Ordered by surviving Court loyalists to kill Pell, Vane instead turns her blade on them, becoming an outlaw in truth. Beat: justice finally divorced from law, at the cost of everything she was.

chapters.title: Hunger Walks Beside Us
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. One of the old gods manifests as a traveling companion, courteous and starving, testing their resolve with gifts and questions. Beat: seduction — power offered gently is still power corrupting.

chapters.title: The Gate of Teeth
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. The party fights through the Court's last army at the Door's threshold. Pell is wounded shielding Mara; Vane holds the pass alone against the Hierophant's guard. Beat: sacrifice as proof of changed hearts.

chapters.title: What Mara Wants to Keep
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. At the Door itself, it demands his dearest possession — and shows him the escape he has dreamed of since childhood: a life beyond the mountains, free, unnamed. Beat: the book's moral crux laid bare.

chapters.title: The Hierophant's Prayer
chapters.summary: Hierophant, POV. Dying, the Hierophant prays not for victory but for the gods to consume the world rather than lose it — and they begin to answer. Beat: villainy as devotion taken to its logical end.

chapters.title: Emberfall
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Climax. Mara steps into the Door and turns the key from within, unmaking the gods' channel — the mountain erupts, the Court burns, and the Door closes behind him into darkness. Beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: On the Other Side of Silence
chapters.summary: Vane, POV. Vane and the wounded Pell wake to a silent, godless Thornfell — freed, grieving, unsure what remains. They find no trace of Mara. Beat: hollow aftermath, mourning without a grave.

chapters.title: The Green Flame's Last Word
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. On the far side, Mara exists half-in, half-out — able to walk the world but bound to its thresholds. He tends a small shrine where prayers go unanswered and are therefore safe. Beat: bittersweet peace; the price accepted.

chapters.title: When the Ember Falls
chapters.summary: Rotating final glimpses: Vane teaching village law again, Pell humming harmlessly to stones, Mara watching snow fall on the closed pass. The ember falls; nothing answers; the country begins again. Beat: resolution — survival's cost honored, corruption broken, justice kept human.
